body:
The diagram below shows how tennis balls are manufactured in a factory, from the mixing of rubber to the packing of the finished product.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Manufacture of tennis balls
steps: Rubber compound is mixed with other materials in an industrial mixer
The mixture is pressed into thin sheets
The sheets are cut into strips and placed in moulds
The moulds are heated to form two hollow rubber halves
The halves are joined and the core is pressurised with gas
Two curved pieces of felt are glued onto the core
The covered balls are pressed in a machine to shape the seam
Balls are checked for size, weight and bounce
Approved balls are sealed in pressurised tubes of three

body:
The diagram below shows the process by which donated blood is tested, separated and stored before it is issued to hospitals.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Processing and storage of donated blood
steps: Whole blood is collected from donors in sterile bags containing an anticoagulant
Each bag is given a unique code and a small sample is taken for testing
Samples are screened in a laboratory for infections and blood group
Bags that fail screening are discarded and the donor is informed
Approved blood is spun in a centrifuge to separate its components
Red cells, plasma and platelets are transferred into separate bags
Empty bags and used tubing are sent for recycling
Plasma is frozen within hours to preserve its clotting factors
Platelets are stored at room temperature and gently agitated
Red cells are chilled and kept in refrigerators for up to 42 days
Components that fail the final quality check are returned for re-testing
Released components are issued to hospitals on request

body:
The maps below show the area around a stadium in 2005 and in 2016, after the city hosted a major sports tournament.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

features: Old stadium in the centre of the site, with a small main stand
Railway station to the west, linked by a footpath
Open car park to the north, next to the river
Derelict warehouses along the eastern edge
Playing fields to the south, used by local schools
Single bus stop on the main road to the south
Stadium in the centre rebuilt with a larger main stand and a roof
Railway station to the west, with a new platform added
Open car park to the north replaced by a six-storey car park
Derelict warehouses on the east demolished and replaced by a hotel
Playing fields to the south converted into a fan zone with screens
Bus stop moved off the main road to a new access road in the north-east corner
New footbridge over the river linking the stadium to housing on the north bank
Tram stop added next to the main entrance on the western side
The main road to the south still forms the boundary of the site

body:
The plans below show a seafront promenade as it is now and as it is planned to look after a redesign with cycle lanes and play areas.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Seafront promenade: current layout and planned redesign

before.label: Now
features: Promenade runs along the whole seafront, with a single footpath
Pier at the centre of the seafront, with a café at its end
Car park at the western end, next to the lifeboat station
Two-lane road along the seafront, used by cars and buses
Public toilets beside the pier
Bandstand on the grass between the pier and the eastern end
Children's playground at the eastern end, next to the beach café
Ice-cream kiosk at the western end, near the car park
Benches along the sea side of the footpath
Beach café beside the eastern playground

after.label: Planned
features: Promenade still runs along the whole seafront, now six metres wide
Café at the end of the pier replaced by a kiosk
Car park at the western end reduced and moved inland, behind the lifeboat station
Two-lane road along the seafront reduced to one lane for buses
Separate two-way cycle lane added along the sea side
Public toilets beside the pier demolished and rebuilt to the west
Children's playground at the eastern end enlarged with a water play area
Bandstand removed to make room for the cycle lane
New skate park added on the former bandstand site
Ice-cream kiosk at the western end moved to the foot of the pier
New trees planted along the landward side of the footpath
Beach café beside the eastern playground, in the same position
